statement: Let z1 be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums1) and nums1[i] = 0, and let b1 = sum_{0 <= i < len(nums1)} nums1[i]. Let z2 be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(nums2) and nums2[j] = 0, and let b2 = sum_{0 <= j < len(nums2)} nums2[j]. The function returns a result r and: (1) if z1 = 0 and z2 = 0, then r = b1 when b1 = b2, and r = -1 when b1 != b2; (2) if z1 = 0 and z2 > 0, then r = b1 when b1 >= b2 + z2, and r = -1 when b1 < b2 + z2; (3) if z1 > 0 and z2 = 0, then r = b2 when b2 >= b1 + z1, and r = -1 when b2 < b1 + z1; (4) if z1 > 0 and z2 > 0, then r = max(b1 + z1, b2 + z2).
preconditions: nums1 and nums2 are slices of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 100000 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000.
